predecessors.name: Byzantine Empire
predecessors.text: the Oristano-Campidano core of western Sardinia, Byzantine Sardinia's 'single archontate' before it fragmented into the judicates

successors.name: Crown of Aragon
successors.text: what remained after Oristano fell in March 1410: Sassari, the capital 1410-1420, and the territory William III of Narbonne sold to Alfonso V for 100,000 gold florins on 14 August 1420

ledger.x: 866 on the bridge: the page is silent.
1070: Orzocorre I moves the capital to Oristano.
June 1326: Pisa's last Sardinian stronghold goes.
1368: Arborea holds almost the whole island.
1388: peace. 'A peace treaty returned the Aragonese their previous possessions in 1388.' The extent returned is the researcher's reading.
1388: the war ends in a peace treaty (the first of two phases).
March 1410: the fighting ends with the fall of Oristano; the Judicate survives only as a remnant until 1420.
14 August 1420: the Judicate of Arborea ends.

wars.name: Mujahid's invasion of Sardinia
wars.outcome: Mujahid landed in 1015, returned in 1016 and defeated the army of the judge of Cagliari, but was driven out in May 1016 by mutiny and the Pisan and Genoese fleets.

wars.name: Aragonese conquest of Sardinia
wars.outcome: Villa di Chiesa surrendered on 7 February 1324, Pisa gave up Cagliari and Gallura on 29 February 1324 keeping Castel di Castro, which passed to the Kingdom of Sardinia in June 1326; Arborea was Aragon's vassal and ally.

wars.name: Arborean-Aragonese wars
wars.outcome: Marianus IV broke the alliance in 1353; the 1368 offensive left the Aragonese Cagliari and Alghero; the 1388 peace returned their possessions; Brancaleone Doria swept most of the island again in 1391; Arborea lost at Sanluri on 30 June 1409 and Oristano fell…

certainty.note: The judicate was divided into 13 or 14 curatoriae but its external frontiers with Cagliari, Logudoro, Gallura and the Aragonese were never delimited on the pages opened; the sea is the only firm edge.
